extracted.intended_audience: Korean Patent Office examiners and patent/utility-model applicants requesting expedited examination
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for determining eligibility and handling of requests for expedited examination of patent and utility model applications under the Korean Patent Act (including grounds such as third-party practice, defense-related, green technology, export promotion, government duties, and venture business status).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of request filed after start of examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Where expedited examination is requested after the start of examination on an application and the application is eligible for expedited examination, an examiner shall recognize the application to have been requested for expedited examination and conduct expedited examination on the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application is eligible even though the request is filed after examination started, the examiner must proceed with expedited examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior-filed application claiming domestic priority (disqualification rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an application requested for expedited examination is a prior-filed application of an application claiming domestic priority, the application is not eligible for expedited examination because the ground for urgent processing under Article 61(2) is not recognized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If confirmed before determination, examiner must order correction (complement the request) within designated period and then dismiss the request after that period. If the priority claim is withdrawn before dismissal, treat the request as valid and conduct expedited examination. If an application becomes a prior-filed application after determination, withhold examination until it is deemed withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application being practiced by a third party (subject inclusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for an invention or utility model deemed to have been practiced as business by a third party after the laying-open of the application shall be included as a subject for expedited examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requester must show that third-party practice occurred after laying-open; see definitions of laying-open, third party, and practicing for details on proof and territorial scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of laying-open of application
rubrics_metrics.description: “Laying-open of application” refers to the publication of an application specified under Article 64 of the Patent Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where an application has not been laid open at the time of request (and early publication not filed or not impending), the applicant shall make a request for early publication; publication status affects whether the expedited ground (third-party practice) can be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of third party
rubrics_metrics.description: “A third party” refers to a person other than an applicant and who has not obtained the permission to practice the claimed invention or utility model.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absent particular grounds, an examiner need not further investigate whether permission was obtained and may accept the requester’s argument as presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of practicing (acts and territoriality)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Practicing” refers to acts listed under Article 2(3) of the Patent Act / Utility Model Act: (a) product inventions — manufacturing, using, assigning, leasing, importing, offering for assignment/lease (including display for that purpose); (b) method inventions — using the method; (c) method-for-manufacturing inventions — manufacturing/using/assigning/leasing/importing/offering for the product manufactured by the method in addition to method use; (d) utility-model-related product acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Practicing’ must occur in the Republic of Korea: practice only in a foreign country does not constitute practicing, but importing a claimed invention produced abroad into Korea does.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of identicalness between practiced invention and claimed invention
rubrics_metrics.description: A requester must clarify that the invention practiced by the third party is identical with the claimed invention and must prove the ground for identicalness of the two inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable proof includes detailed descriptions of time/place/product name/sales numbers, photographs of the product with explanatory description (time/date of purchase, correlation to claimed invention), content-certified mail, other evidential documents or the product itself. Examiner compares submitted materials (products/pictures) to the claimed invention; if identicalness cannot be determined from submitted materials, examiner may order supplementation. If high possibility exists and requester cannot obtain cooperation from the practicing person, examiner may recognize the request without additional materials unless it is obvious the two are substantially not the same; if different, dismiss the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of requests based on practicing prior to laying-open
rubrics_metrics.description: When requesting expedited examination based on third-party practice before laying-open, the application should be laid open as of the date of determination on expedited examination; request for early publication may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If publication is imminent (expected within 15 days of transmittal of written request) or applicant requested early publication, examiner shall defer determination on expedited examination without dismissal. Once laid open, conduct expedited examination. If early publication is dismissed and application is not to be laid open early, the deferred decision may lead to dismissal per normal rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling requests in presence of warning from applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who received a warning letter about practicing the published invention without permission may request expedited examination by submitting the written warning or copy plus a detailed explanation (date, means, contents, relation to claimed invention).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner shall recognize the request provided there is no special ground for the applicant’s rejection of the fact that a warning was delivered and the practiced invention is not clearly different from the claimed invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defense industry subject inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications related to the defense industry and applications on defense materials or manufacturing processes defined under Article 34 of the Defense Acquisition Program Act (and related Enforcement Decree/Rules) are subjects for expedited examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defense materials are divided into major defense materials (e.g., firearms, guided weapons, aircraft, radars, night observation, CBRN equipment, command systems designated as important) and general defense materials (other defense materials).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination guidelines for defense industry applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for expedited examination on an application related to the defense industry does not require submission of additional evidential documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A requester may indicate the name of at least one of the items listed under the Directive (example given) in a written explanation and explain that the claimed invention constitutes the concerned item. If the examiner can determine the subject matter falls under the defense materials definitions even if the requester did not specify exactly, the examiner may recognize the request without making a correction order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: patent applications directly related to green technology / pollution prevention
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for expedited examination a claimed invention shall constitute green technology (including pollution prevention technologies); green technology broadly refers to technologies that minimize greenhouse gases and pollutants by saving/efficiently using energy across socioeconomic activities (examples listed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When requesting expedited examination on green technology, requester must explain on what ground the claimed invention constitutes green technology in the written explanation. Determination is made based on the applicant’s argument. A long list of example initiatives and technologies (27 major initiatives and items from 17 new growth engines) are explicitly considered green technology. If no explanation is given or invention deemed irrelevant, examiner shall order correction of the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Green technology financed or certified by the State (eligible grounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent applications directly related to green technology financed or certified by the State (per Article 4(2)(b)) are eligible for expedited examination if they meet one of enumerated grounds (certified as green technology; filed by certified green business; subsidized by State/local governments; received investment from Green Technology Investment Co.; applicant stationed in Green Technology Industrial Cluster; financed/certified based on other national policies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner decides based on the requester’s explanation that the claimed invention constitutes green technology and is financed/certified by the State etc. Examiner must check submitted evidential documents by each ground and verify that the applicant and claimed invention correspond to the person/technology that got the support/certification. Refer to the Green Technology-related Evidential Documents table for required items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required evidential documents for green technology financing/certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific evidential documents are required depending on the ground for request: green technology certification, green business, subsidization, investment from Green Technology Industry Co., being stationed in a Green Technology Industrial Cluster, or other financial support/certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: certification of green technology under Article 32; explanation verifying claimed invention and business belong to same industry; evidential document of subsidization from State/local governments; evidential document of receiving investments (loan statement); evidence of being stationed in industrial cluster; documents such as R&D financing announcements, loan statements, environmental mark/carbon footprint/new technology certifications, GR certification, or other financial support/certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications on pollution prevention facilities and methods (subject list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications whose primary purpose is to prevent or eliminate pollution and which relate to designated environmental pollution prevention facilities or the methods those facilities hold (e.g., noise/vibration control, water pollution preventive facility, air pollution control equipment, waste disposal facilities, resource-conversion/sanitation/public disposal, recycling facilities, public sewage/waste treatment plants).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilities falling under environment-related acts are enumerated; certain facilities (e.g., those eliminating malodors or specific annexed forms) are treated as air pollution control equipment where indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination guidelines for pollution prevention facility applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Where expedited examination is requested on the ground of an application related to designated pollution prevention facilities, the requester does not need to submit additional evidential documents and need only indicate in the written explanation that the application falls under one of the specified subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If requester vaguely indicates 'a patent application useful for pollution prevention', the examiner may recognize the request if the examiner deems it corresponds to the designated facilities. If the application does not fall under the designated facilities, it shall not be eligible even if useful for pollution prevention; medical agents or living organisms used for facility operation are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-eligibility example for pollution prevention (scope nuance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if a claimed invention directly reduces emissions, it is not eligible if the facility is not one of the pollution prevention facilities designated under the environment-related acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a car is not a designated air pollutant emitter under the Clean Air Conservation Act Annex; an exhaust gas converter installed within a car is therefore not eligible for expedited examination because it does not correspond to the designated air pollution prevention facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications directly related to promotion of export (evidence and identicalness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications directly related to promotion of export may be eligible; determination requires review of evidential documents such as statement of export result, arrival of letter of credit (L/C), purchaser's necessity documents, export contract, documents showing adoption to international standards, or other evidence that invention is directly related to trade promotion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The invention to be exported and the claimed invention must be identical. The requester must prove identicalness; where identicalness normally cannot be determined solely from request documents, the examiner may recognize the request without requiring additional evidence if there is a high possibility they are the same and no grounds to doubt it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications related to duties of state or municipal governments (eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications related to duties of state or municipal governments (including duties of national or public schools and organizations exclusively responsible for tech transfer/commercialization set up in such schools) are subjects for expedited examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request is valid only when made by the state/municipal governments (or the designated organization). If requester is not one of these, examiner must order correction within a designated period and dismiss if not corrected. National/public school duty applications filed by the designated organization are treated the same as state/municipal government applications. Organizations must be legal entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications related to companies certified as venture businesses (eligibility rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications of businesses confirmed as venture businesses under the Act on Special Measures for Promotion of Venture Businesses are eligible under specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examination guidelines include: (i) joint filing where at least one applicant is a venture business -> accept; (ii) identical names of certified venture company and applicant -> accept; (iii) at least one of filing date / date of expedited request / date of determination must be within the valid period on the venture certificate; (iv) original copy of confirmation used to verify venture status (copies may be acceptable if recognized as same); (v) a written notice of evaluation result cannot replace the confirmation. (Further procedural points may follow beyond the provided text.)
